units.objective: Explain a mark using mixture concentration, brush load and paper condition separately.

exercise.action: Make the two load-test strokes above. Beside them, name which control changed and which two you kept similar.
constants: Dry paper of the same type
success: You can name the changed control without calling it dilution.
You can describe a visible difference or a useful inconclusive result.
exercise.transfer: Before a sky, petal or architectural wash, name the palette, brush and surface conditions separately.

units.objective: Arrange a small, stable working area and enough mixture for an uninterrupted passage.

exercise.action: Without touching paint to paper yet, rehearse moving from the puddle to the rectangle and back. Reduce the planned rectangle if the reach is awkward; leave the palette in place.
success: The sheet stays stable.
You can reach mixture, clean water and wiping material without crossing the painted passage.
exercise.transfer: Prepare the largest connected wash of your next subject before beginning it.

units.objective: Repeat a loading action that produces a usable stroke without an uncontrolled final drop.

exercise.action: Make a row of three similar strokes, reloading before each. Keep the puddle unchanged and repeat the same unloading action.
exercise.variable: Loading action during initial adjustment; then repeat it
success: At least two strokes have comparable delivery.
You can identify whether any problem appears at the start, middle or end.
exercise.transfer: Use a scrap stroke before laying a clean light passage in your painting.

previews.believedTopic: Broad brush/wash viewing proposal, not an isolated loading clip.
previews.requiresDirectVerification: Locate actual wetting, belly loading, unloading and result context within the owner’s longer proposal; those actions are not individually witnessed in this record.

units.objective: Change mark width deliberately while separating contact pressure from liquid load.

exercise.action: Compare the two rows. Change only the amount of hair in contact with the paper; keep the colour and loading sequence unchanged.
success: A narrow and a broader mark are distinguishable.
You can make both without flattening the hairs against the ferrule.
exercise.transfer: Use tip contact for a selected stem or edge and broader contact for the supporting mass.

units.objective: Connect successive passes and finish without dragging a puddle through a drying area.

exercise.action: Paint one small rectangle using connected passes from the same mixture. On fresh scrap, repeat after adjusting only the load if the first wash pooled.
exercise.variable: Brush load, only between fresh attempts
success: Most adjacent passes connect without a dry gap.
The final edge is left without an uncontrolled pool, or you can identify why you stopped.
exercise.transfer: Use the wet-edge decision for a quiet sky or a single broad colour shape, without requiring every surface to be perfectly smooth.

previews.believedTopic: The same longer wash proposal, not a newly verified short wash segment.
previews.requiresDirectVerification: Confirm the actual pass sequence, wet bead and final result; no brush-action sub-boundaries have been supplied.

units.objective: Produce distinguishable dry values while keeping brush delivery reasonably comparable.

exercise.action: Complete both three-swatch rows. Label the three concentrations in order after they dry, and circle any pair that is too similar to judge confidently.
constants: Swatch size and dry starting surface
success: Three dry value groups are recognisable, or a specific repeat test is planned.
Wet and dry swatches are not compared as if their conditions were equal.
exercise.transfer: Select a tested light or middle mixture for a petal, building plane or landscape passage.

units.objective: Describe moisture from visible conditions rather than elapsed seconds.

exercise.action: Write down two surface states as the scrap dries and predict how a stroke might spread in each. Keep this patch untouched; use the next dry/damp comparison to test the prediction on fresh areas.
success: You distinguish standing water from an evenly damp surface.
You do not treat lost sheen as permission to scrub a partly drying wash.
exercise.transfer: Read a sky or foliage passage before deciding whether to connect another shape or leave it alone.

previews.believedTopic: Owner-screened blending topic, beginning at 1:30; the endpoint is unknown.
previews.requiresDirectVerification: Establish the complete moisture sequence and its endpoint without inferring dry or damp conditions from the title.

units.objective: Connect an observed surface condition to a changed edge and spread.

exercise.action: Complete the dry/damp pair. Describe one observed condition and its boundary, without calling every soft transition a lost edge.
success: Both conditions are recorded, including an inconclusive difference.
You distinguish a soft transition from a genuinely disappearing contour.
exercise.transfer: Try the same comparison on a simple hill, leaf or abstract shape before using it in a painting.

previews.believedTopic: Publisher’s wet-on-wet chapter hint; suggested comparison context only.
previews.requiresDirectVerification: Inspect actual surface moisture, load, spread and result; published chapter boundaries are not certified instructional clips.

previews.believedTopic: Publisher’s wet-on-dry chapter hint; compare with the separate wet-on-wet proposal.
previews.requiresDirectVerification: Inspect the actual dry-paper demonstration, setup and result. This is not evidence of a lost edge.

units.objective: Use a visible symptom to select a plausible cause and a fresh controlled experiment.

exercise.action: Write a symptom, a plausible cause, the condition you checked and the single variable for a fresh repeat. Make the repeat only if the surface and materials are ready.
exercise.variable: One selected cause at a time
constants: All controls other than the selected one
success: The proposed cause is conditional, not certain from appearance alone.
You can explain when to stop instead of disturbing the current passage.
exercise.transfer: Use a margin or separate scrap to test a correction before applying it to an important painting.

units.objective: Name one observed relationship, one remaining uncertainty and a small real-painting application.

exercise.action: Use the existing reflection field to record a relationship, a condition to repeat, an uncertainty and a small application to your own subject.
exercise.variable: Chosen handling in a new shape
constants: The tested mixture or loading sequence where useful
success: The reflection refers to visible evidence, not a guessed hidden process.
The proposed transfer names a physical action and an observation.
exercise.transfer: Use the chosen decision in the next guided landscape or your own subject; keep the other controls simple.

units.objective: Identify three large value families without using hue as a substitute for lightness.

exercise.action: Make three small pencil patches beside your sketch and assign one visible mass to each. Check the order against your subject.
success: Three relative families are named without relying on hue.
Any uncertain grouping is identified rather than forced.
exercise.transfer: Use the same comparison before choosing the first mixture for another subject.

previews.believedTopic: Owner-screened value overview, not a precise clip of this still life. Viewing is additional to the short study.
previews.requiresDirectVerification: Confirm the actual grouping decisions and surrounding context within the unchanged 37–852s owner proposal; no new action boundaries are inferred.

units.objective: Prepare two matching small frames and three working values before adding details.

exercise.action: Prepare both frames and a three-value key. Compare their major silhouettes before filling either frame.
success: Both frames describe the same placement.
The intended light remains legible before dark accents are added.
exercise.transfer: Use a light-shape map to protect paper white in a sky, petal or building.

units.objective: Complete a readable first plan with three dominant families and no small descriptive detail.

exercise.action: Finish the first three-family plan. Point to its main light, middle and dark at arm's length and name the first point of attention.
success: Large masses remain readable.
You can explain the emphasis without naming a compulsory darkest focal point.
exercise.transfer: Protect those broad relationships when you make a colour study.

units.objective: Compare two intentions while keeping crop, large shapes and overall dark area similar.

exercise.action: Complete the alternative plan and write one sentence connecting the moved accent with an observed change in attention.
exercise.variable: Position of one small dark accent
success: One meaningful change can be identified.
Your preference refers to an intention, or you explain why both remain useful.
exercise.transfer: Try an alternative emphasis cheaply before committing dark paint to a larger study.

units.objective: Retain a useful value decision and one question for a later painting.

exercise.action: Use the original reflection controls to name the changed relationship, its effect and one colour application. No video is required for this decision.
success: The reflection identifies an observed difference.
A next test names a practical decision rather than a universal value rule.
exercise.transfer: Apply the plan to a landscape, urban mass or a single observed leaf.

units.objective: Distinguish a hard boundary, a soft transition and a locally lost contour.

exercise.action: Name three intervals in the comparison and choose one edge relationship for your own small shape.
success: Soft and lost are distinguished.
The chosen edge has an intended job.
exercise.transfer: Use the same reading when deciding which contour matters in a sky, petal or street.

units.objective: Paint a definite boundary without scrubbing a setting edge.

exercise.action: Paint and leave the baseline shape. Describe one dry boundary interval without claiming every material makes the same edge.
success: A relatively abrupt interval can be identified.
The drying shape is left undisturbed.
exercise.transfer: Use a dry-paper boundary for a selected roof, leaf tip or near mass when it serves the intention.

previews.believedTopic: Publisher's wet-on-dry chapter hint; exact brush and surface actions remain unverified.
previews.requiresDirectVerification: Inspect the actual dry-paper setup and boundary before approving this as an exact hard-edge demonstration.

units.objective: Make a gradual boundary while keeping concentration and brush delivery reasonably similar.

exercise.action: Compare the dry hard/soft pair and record the actual surface condition you observed. Keep an inconclusive comparison as evidence too.
success: One gradual transition is identified or a specific fresh test is planned.
A visible soft boundary is not called lost.
exercise.transfer: Try the same relationship on a supporting hill or leaf passage before applying it to a larger painting.

previews.believedTopic: Publisher's wet-on-wet chapter hint, related to diffusion rather than proof of a lost contour.
previews.requiresDirectVerification: Inspect actual paper condition, delivery and resulting edge. No lost-edge claim is supported by this mapping.

units.objective: Create a short genuinely disappearing contour while retaining enough information for the form to read.

exercise.action: Complete a merging pair and a small application. Name the interval that disappeared and the found edge that keeps the form readable.
success: A truly disappearing interval is distinguished from soft visibility.
The application still communicates a form or mass.
exercise.transfer: Use the relationship where neighbouring foliage, petals or land masses can share a value.

units.objective: Connect a dry boundary relationship with the visual job it should do in another subject.

exercise.action: Record one deliberate pairing of found and quieter edges and a physical next-use plan. No video is needed to complete this reflection.
exercise.variable: Boundary treatment in a new subject
constants: A tested handling condition where useful
success: The next application names both purpose and action.
Softness is not substituted for proof of a lost contour.
exercise.transfer: Use that pairing in the landscape project or a subject you have observed.

units.objective: Compare a subject's large width, height and placement from one fixed viewpoint.

exercise.action: Draw one small outer envelope and mark its main corner. Check one width/height relationship against your subject.
success: The large extents have been compared.
One uncertain proportion is named rather than concealed by detail.
exercise.transfer: Use the same check before painting a street mass, boat or botanical silhouette.

units.objective: Record the principal plane boundaries and re-observe one related pair of receding edges.

exercise.action: Complete the first few-line study and mark one truly related receding pair for the next comparison.
success: A related edge pair is identified.
Other diagonals are not forced toward that pair's point.
exercise.transfer: Use the group check before adding selective structural lines in an urban wash.

previews.believedTopic: Research mapping for observed structure. No exact instructional window or duration has been verified.
previews.requiresDirectVerification: Inspect narration, related edge grouping and level before defining any precise segment. Original-video access only; do not infer footage from its title.

units.objective: Make a second study that isolates one structural change or explains an intentional distortion.

exercise.action: Complete the second study, identify the changed pair and explain one observed or expressive consequence.
success: One structural change can be identified.
A remaining distortion is either intentional or named for a later test.
exercise.transfer: Carry only the necessary structure into a small urban colour study.

units.objective: Name an assumption replaced by observation and a practical check for the next painting.

exercise.action: Record one changed relationship, one deliberate choice and one next-use check. No video is needed for this reflection.
exercise.variable: Observation habit applied to a new subject
constants: A fixed viewpoint for each separate study
success: The next check names an action and an observation.
Expressive choice and uncertain measurement remain distinct.
exercise.transfer: Use the check before the next landscape structure, street corner or still life.

units.objective: State a visual intention and identify the light space and small landing that support it.

exercise.action: Prepare the small sheet and choose one sentence of intention, one open light and one restrained landing.
success: An intention is named.
The open space has a purpose before details are planned.
exercise.transfer: Use the same intention-led start for a boat, street mass or abstract landscape.

units.objective: Make a small value plan that preserves the main light and separates the two land masses deliberately.

exercise.action: Complete the small three-family plan and identify one light shape that the painting must preserve.
success: The large groups read at a distance.
A specific open light and quieter interval are planned.
exercise.transfer: Keep the plan beside the painting as a decision aid, while still responding to actual dry results.

previews.believedTopic: The same 37–852s owner proposal used in value planning; not a demonstration of this generated landscape.
previews.requiresDirectVerification: Inspect the actual value grouping and surrounding context before identifying any project-specific or shorter clip.

units.objective: Test the light/middle relationships, brush delivery and a safe drying pause before starting the sky.

exercise.action: Dry-test the pale and middle relationships and rehearse one connected sky pass. Mark the intended drying pause on the plan.
exercise.variable: Selected sky concentration during the swatch test
success: The light mixture is chosen from a dry comparison.
A stopping/drying decision is explicit.
exercise.transfer: Use the same preparation before a large connected colour shape in another subject.

previews.believedTopic: The same broad 47–702s wash proposal, offered here for preparation rather than as a newly certified sky clip.
previews.requiresDirectVerification: Confirm the actual loading/pass sequence and context. No new short bounds or exact-action claims are introduced.

units.objective: Establish a simple connected sky while preserving the planned light space.

exercise.action: Paint the small light sky passage and pause. Note the surface condition and whether the planned light remains open.
exercise.variable: Sky handling within the chosen plan
success: A broad light mass remains.
A drying passage is left without repeated scrubbing.
exercise.transfer: Use the same stopping judgement in a light background or pale petal wash.

previews.believedTopic: Publisher's 439–725s practice chapter hint for a related sky topic. The conflicting 138s hints are not used.
previews.requiresDirectVerification: Inspect the actual paper condition, preserved lights, pacing and narration before approving any technique match. This is not the app's landscape being painted.

units.objective: Make the hill readable while keeping its value and selected boundary subordinate to the intended landing.

exercise.action: Place one connected hill using the safe surface option you tested. Record the observed condition and the relationship with the light sky.
success: The hill remains readable.
The selected handling does not rely on scrubbing the sky into submission.
exercise.transfer: Use a tested boundary option for any supporting mass behind a clearer focal shape.

units.objective: Establish a coherent nearer group with one chosen clearer interval and a quieter supporting interval.

exercise.action: Paint one connected bank, inspect the relationship dry, and choose whether any texture is needed. Preserve one clearer and one quieter interval.
exercise.variable: Near-mass relationship chosen from the plan
success: The bank reads before its small details.
Any added texture has a named visual job.
exercise.transfer: Build a connected foliage, street-shadow or still-life mass before breaking it into small descriptions.

units.objective: Choose to stop or make one justified, tested adjustment without sacrificing relationships that already work.

exercise.action: Choose to stop or perform one tested adjustment. Record its intended job; a decision to stop is a complete response to this stage.
success: The decision has a reason.
Effective light and middle relationships are preserved.
exercise.transfer: Use the same test-before-mark habit on an urban, botanical or expressive study.

units.objective: Compare intention, plan and dry result, naming one useful relationship and one separate future test.

exercise.action: Complete the original reflection with an observed relationship, a condition to repeat and a separate future test.
exercise.variable: One choice reserved for a new study
constants: Comparable main design if testing a hill edge
success: The reflection refers to visible evidence.
The next test identifies an action and an observation, not a claim of mastery.
exercise.transfer: Carry the principle into your own landscape, boat, street or abstract arrangement.
